Put the main subject and visible attributes in subject; clothing and accessories in appearance; hair and makeup in hair_makeup; body position and action in pose; visible facial expression in expression; setting and background in environment; framing, viewpoint, and depth of field in composition; visible light quality, direction, and color in lighting; and observable color grading or photographic finish in finishing. # Qwen3.5-9B → Krea2 Image to Text Save
1. Download [Qwen3.5-9B BF16](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen3.5/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_bf16.safetensors) into `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/` and select it in Load CLIP.
2. Select an image in Load Image, then run the workflow. The instruction asks for a photo-inspired `title` of 1–24 ASCII letters, digits, or `!#$%*+-./:;=?@_~`, with underscores instead of spaces.
3. Inspect the generated JSON and the nine fields on Krea2 Image to Text Save. If `photo_id` is blank, the node uses the JSON `title` as the proposed Photo ID. An entered or connected `photo_id` takes precedence. With Manual mode, click **Save** to register the proposed Photo ID. Change to Auto to save during each run.
4. Use Krea2 Photo Prompt Reference to reuse a saved Photo ID. If JSON validation fails, rerun or adjust the instruction.
Requires a recent ComfyUI with the built-in TextGenerate node and this custom node package. The model is about 19.3 GB. The workflow does not download it or include a sample image.

# Image analysis instruction example
The following instruction is already set in the `TextGenerate` node. Copy or edit it as needed.

```text
Analyze the input photograph and return exactly one valid JSON object. Output JSON only: no Markdown fences, introduction, explanation, or text after the object. Use exactly these ten keys in this order, with string values: "title", "subject", "appearance", "hair_makeup", "pose", "expression", "environment", "composition", "lighting", "finishing". Choose a title that reflects the impression of the photograph. Make the title 1 to 24 characters long; use only ASCII letters, digits, and these permitted half-width symbols: ! # $ % * + - . / : ; = ? @ _ ~. Use underscores (_) instead of spaces in the title. Write concise, concrete English descriptions useful as a photographic image-generation prompt. Describe only details visible in the image; do not invent identity, intent, camera model, lens focal length, or editing settings. Put the main subject and visible attributes in subject; clothing and accessories in appearance; hair and makeup in hair_makeup; body position and action in pose; visible facial expression in expression; setting and background in environment; framing, viewpoint, and depth of field in composition; visible light quality, direction, and color in lighting; and observable color grading or photographic finish in finishing. Use an empty string when a photo prompt category cannot be determined. Include the title and all nine photo prompt fields even when some field values are empty. Escape quotation marks and newlines inside JSON strings.
```

## Example JSON for `tags_json`
```json
{
  "title": "Urban_Street_Portrait",
  "subject": "One adult person",
  "appearance": "White shirt and dark jacket",
  "hair_makeup": "Short dark hair",
  "pose": "Standing and facing the camera",
  "expression": "Neutral expression",
  "environment": "City street in the background",
  "composition": "Waist-up portrait, eye-level viewpoint, blurred background",
  "lighting": "Soft daylight from camera left",
  "finishing": "Muted colors"
}
```

Return one JSON object without code fences. Include `title` and all nine photo prompt fields, with string values. The title must be 1–24 characters and use only ASCII letters, digits, or `!#$%*+-./:;=?@_~`; replace spaces with underscores. Use an empty string for any photo prompt field that cannot be determined from the image. Keep at least one photo prompt field nonempty and each field value at or below 8000 characters. When `photo_id` is blank, the save node uses `title` as its Photo ID.
